blurb: Lively white British terrier in two coats, smooth and wire, bred to bolt foxes
description: The Fox Terrier is a small British terrier type in two breeds, Smooth and Wire, mostly white with tan or black markings, bred to drive foxes from their dens.
answer: Fox Terrier is the name for two closely related British terrier breeds, the Smooth Fox Terrier and the Wire Fox Terrier, which differ mainly in coat. Both stand about 36 to 39 cm tall and weigh roughly 6.8 to 8.6 kg, and were originally bred to drive foxes out of their dens for hunting packs.

body: Both breeds developed in 19th-century England from a handful of dogs descended from earlier British terriers. The earliest recorded white terrier was Pitch, owned by Colonel Thomas Thornton in 1790. The Beagle, Old English Bulldog, English Toy Terrier, Pointer and even Dalmatian are thought to have contributed. Complete pedigrees exist from 1870, with the dogs Old Jock, Trap and Tartar behind most modern lines.

Fox Terriers ran with packs of English Foxhounds, but as they were bred longer-legged for speed they became too big for their original work. The Fox Terrier Club of England was founded in 1876. The Fox Terrier has won more Best in Show titles at Westminster than any other breed, and the AKC has treated Smooth and Wire as separate breeds since 1985.

Both types are mostly white with coloured piebald markings, most often tan and black, and have small dark eyes and V-shaped ears. The Smooth Fox Terrier has a short, hard coat and a long, wedge-shaped head. The Wire Fox Terrier has a hard, crisp, dense double coat whose hairs twist but do not curl, and a body shorter than it is tall. Descendant breeds include the Jack Russell Terrier, Miniature Fox Terrier, Rat Terrier and Toy Fox Terrier.

The source text says little about temperament. As terriers bred to work with hounds and go after foxes, Fox Terriers are generally associated with energy and a strong hunting drive; breed clubs and the breed standards give fuller descriptions.
Sources give little specific care guidance. As active working terriers, they are generally expected to need regular exercise, and the wire coat typically needs more grooming than the smooth coat.

The average lifespan is given as around 15 years, and a Kennel Club survey reported a median age at death of 13 years and 2 months, with old age and cancer as the leading causes. Conditions reported include myasthenia gravis and cataracts in the Smooth Fox Terrier, megaesophagus and atopic dermatitis in the Wire Fox Terrier, and allergies in both.

faq.q: What is the difference between a Smooth and a Wire Fox Terrier?
faq.a: They are essentially the same in build and size; the Smooth has a short, hard coat, while the Wire has a dense, crisp, wiry double coat.

faq.q: How long do Fox Terriers live?
faq.a: The average lifespan is around 15 years, and a Kennel Club survey reported a median age at death of 13 years and 2 months.

faq.q: How big does a Fox Terrier get?
faq.a: Both types typically stand about 36 to 39 cm at the withers and weigh about 6.8 to 8.6 kg.
